objectives.text: Take the state in Khartoum by force and replace the army-led government with its own. The RSF built a parallel Government of Peace and Unity (charter signed in Nairobi in Feb 2025, announced by Hemedti on 15 Apr 2025, seat Nyala). On 22 Sep 2026 Reuters reported Hemedti telling his troops that the time for fighting had come. The aim is the state, not a truce: its humanitarian truce of 6 Nov 2025 was a tactical pause.

objectives.text: Hold Darfur and open the road to Kordofan and El Obeid. Losing Kordofan would cut the RSF off from the centre, so the western and southern front is where the objective is decided.

means.text: Gold. The RSF seized key mines, the Sudan Gold Refinery and control of gold processing and exports through the RSF-linked Al Gunade company. Smuggled gold reaches the UAE, the main buyer, by routes through Libya, Chad, South Sudan and Egypt, with Dubai as the entry point. Gold revenue finances the war; the figures are reported, not audited.

constraints.text: No recognised state and no sovereign routes. The parallel government is rejected by the African Union, the Arab League and most of the region, and the RSF has neither port nor airspace of its own: every reported supply line runs through a third state (Chad, eastern Libya, Ethiopia). Those doors can close: Chad shut its eastern border on 23 Feb 2026 and Kufra airport was shut for a month in Jan 2026.

constraints.text: Exposure to atrocity findings and sanctions. The US determined on 7 Jan 2025 that the RSF and allied militias committed genocide and sanctioned Hemedti; the El Fasher capture of Oct 2025 was followed by reports that more than 2,000 civilians were executed and by satellite images of burial and burning. Any patron that backs the RSF openly pays for it, and the record closes the Western door to any settlement that leaves the RSF with power.

paradoxes.text: The patron that arms the RSF is the reason it cannot be recognised. Abu Dhabi supplies the RSF, but the UAE is inside the Quad and Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the AU reject the parallel government as the UAE's creature. The more the UAE backs the RSF, the less the RSF can become a state, and the truce it accepts (6 Nov 2025) is one it negotiated through the same Quad.

paradoxes.text: Territory taken by massacre cannot be governed. El Fasher (Oct 2025) gave the RSF the army's last Darfur base and control of almost all of Darfur, but the atrocities made the genocide finding the frame of any settlement, and the army has since retaken Kordofan towns and claims momentum. A state needs the population it has terrorised; the means it used to take the territory are the ones that stop it from holding the state.

grand_strategy.reading:
The RSF is a militia that has tried to become a state: it took Darfur and the gold fields, and it declared its own government in 2025, but it has no recognition, its supply runs through the neighbours of Sudan, and the El Fasher record has made the genocide finding the frame of any settlement.
On the Luttwak reading its central paradox is that the patron that makes it strong, the UAE, is also the reason it cannot be recognised, and the army's retaking of Kordofan since January 2026 shows that a massacre can take territory without making a state.
Its truces are tactical pauses, not a change of aim, so the state in Khartoum remains the objective and the war continues.

stances.note: Mortal enemy on both sides, read from the RSF side. The army's aim is the RSF's destruction (Burhan rejects any truce that leaves the militia in place), and the RSF's aim is the state in Khartoum: the parallel Government of Peace and Unity (announced 15 Apr 2025, seat Nyala) and Hemedti's call to fight again (Reuters, 22 Sep 2026). The humanitarian truce the RSF declared on 6 Nov 2025 was a tactical pause. Mirror of the SDN stance toward nsa-rsf, same sources. Bond grievance: the RSF grew out of the state's own force, a betrayal wound, not a kin tie.

sources.title: Reuters: Drone strikes cut power across southeast Sudan, operator says
